correctness.rationale: The nonidentity vertices split into the transversal clique \(Q^*\) and clique blocks \(B_L=(L\setminus\{1\})\times Q\), one for each order-\(p\) line \(L\le C_p^d\). Distinct \(B_L\) have no edges between them, while \(Q^*\) sees exactly the mixed-order vertices in each block. Each block contains pure order-\(p\) vertices with no external neighbors, forcing every dominating set to meet all \(t\) blocks. One mixed generator per block attains ordinary domination. A size-\(t\) selector has no selected neighbor across blocks, so total domination needs one additional \(Q^*\) vertex and \(t+1\) is sharp. In any paired dominating set, a matching edge can serve selected vertices from at most one required block, forcing at least \(t\) matching edges; two mixed generators per block attain \(2t\). The argument covers \(d=1\) and all distinct prime orientations because \(\varphi(pq)=(p-1)(q-1)\ge2\).
correctness.risk: The formulas use the elementary-abelian \(p\)-factor and prime cyclic \(q\)-factor essentially; no extension to higher prime powers is established.

final_claim: For distinct primes \(p,q\), \(d\ge1\), and \(G\cong C_p^d\times C_q\), if \(t=(p^d-1)/(p-1)\), then the proper power graph satisfies \(\gamma=t\), \(\gamma_t=t+1\), and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}=2t\); hence \(\gamma_t-\gamma=1\) while \(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}}-\gamma=t\) is unbounded with \(d\).
limitations: Ordinary domination is substantially covered by prior work; originality is concentrated in total/paired domination and the gap.
